title: Broker session: Job ownership, core delegation, STARTED after proof, natural COMPLETED
description:
SPIDR child 3c of 4, split from task-af3d7bc8af2146cf92d98557ed0e90c0 by architect-5aba94da. Human confirmed the 4-way split in the REPL. Carries parent DoD items 3 and 4.

DEPENDS ON task-05bf0e0fe7e84afb8584588ecf96db14 (3a: package, descriptors) and task-14ab762db8494959b93b070b9d3b3730 (3b: protocol vocabularies and framing). Do not start until BOTH are DONE, and RE-MEASURE their landed symbols before planning -- every prior task in this chain found a stale claim in its own description.

Objective: hold the Job, drive the core, and never publish a status frame the core has not actually proved.

Deliverable, inside packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/broker/:
- src/session.rs (NEW): owns the SOLE dedicated Job handle for one launch, builds the core's ProcessSpec from the validated launch request, duplicates only fd3/4/5 into the inherited allowlist, and delegates every Win32 operation to moe-windows-job-core. No Job or process syscall is restated here.
- src/main.rs: wire descriptors (3a) plus protocol (3b) plus session into the actual broker loop.
- tests/session.rs (NEW): scripted-call-table tests over the ordering guarantees below.

STARTED IS EARNED, NOT ANNOUNCED. It may be emitted on fd1 only after the core has proved, in order: exact Job limit flags, explicit assignment, membership, retained-handle process identity, and one successful resume. The core already returns each of these as a distinct fact; the session must consume those facts rather than infer success from the absence of an error. A test must fail each proof arm in turn and assert that STARTED never reaches fd1 -- absence from the recorded output, not merely that an error was returned.

NATURAL COMPLETION HAS FOUR PRECONDITIONS, ALL REQUIRED before handles close and COMPLETED is emitted: the retained root handle is waited, the exit is queried exactly, provider fd4 and fd5 reach EOF, and the Job reports ActiveProcesses==0. Any leg whose outcome is uncertain keeps the result UNKNOWN and must never be upgraded to COMPLETED. Note the core deliberately makes an exit code unconstructible without a confirmed signalled wait -- consume that type, do not work around it.

TERMINATION PATHS, each of which must terminate and reap EXACTLY ONCE and preserve UNKNOWN on any uncertain leg: CANCEL received on fd0, an instructed timeout, fd0 EOF, malformed control arriving AFTER a successful launch, and helper shutdown. Idempotence UNDER CONCURRENCY is 3d's, but each path individually terminating once is this task's.

NOT IN SCOPE: descriptor acquisition (3a), frame codec and vocabularies (3b), concurrent-idempotence and forcible-kill grandchild proofs and the final acceptance sweep (3d). No JavaScript, no daemon/store, no receipts, no public @moe/runner export.

Verification: cargo test --locked --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker && cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/Cargo.toml --target-dir dist/windows-job-native -p moe-windows-job-broker
definitionOfDone: STARTED reaches fd1 only after the core has proved exact Job limit flags, explicit assignment, membership, retained-handle process identity, and one successful resume. Proved by failing each of those arms in turn and asserting STARTED is ABSENT from the recorded fd1 output for every one -- absence from the stream, never merely that an error was returned.

The session owns the sole dedicated Job handle for a launch and restates no Win32 Job or process syscall: every such operation is delegated to moe-windows-job-core. Verified by grep that the broker contains no CreateJobObject, AssignProcessToJobObject, CreateProcessW, ResumeThread, TerminateProcess or WaitForSingleObject call site of its own.

COMPLETED is emitted only after ALL FOUR preconditions hold: the retained root handle waited, the exit queried exactly, provider fd4 and fd5 at EOF, and Job ActiveProcesses==0. Each precondition is failed independently in a test asserting COMPLETED is absent and the result stays UNKNOWN by its stable reason code -- four separate tests, not one combined path.
Every refusal frame emitted by the session carries only the exact stable operation and numeric Win32 code, never executable, argv, cwd, environment or handle data and never a free-form string.

Each of the five termination paths -- CANCEL on fd0, instructed timeout, fd0 EOF, malformed control after a successful launch, and helper shutdown -- terminates and reaps EXACTLY ONCE, asserted by a call-count table per path, and preserves UNKNOWN on any leg whose outcome could not be observed. Five distinct call-log assertions; a single shared path satisfying all five fails this item.

An exit code is never reported without the core's confirmed signalled-wait proof: the session consumes the core's type rather than reconstructing a code from a raw query. Verified by a test that supplies a still-running process and asserts the UNKNOWN reason code rather than a number.

Every Rust production source is <=250 physical lines by `grep -c ''` with counts recorded; the locked broker test and release build both exit 0; no executable, Cargo target output, transcript or generated smoke evidence is committed.
taskRails: The helper owns the sole dedicated Job handle. Closing it is crash safety, NOT success evidence: ordinary completion and cancel must query ActiveProcesses==0 before returning authority-neutral completion.

Delegate every Win32 lifecycle operation to moe-windows-job-core. Restating a Job or process syscall in the broker is a rail violation even where it looks simpler, and is separately checkable by grep.
STARTED, COMPLETED and REFUSED are earned from proved facts. Never infer success from the absence of an error, and never upgrade an UNKNOWN leg.
Refusals carry the closed operation vocabulary and a numeric Win32 code only; never echo executable, argv, cwd, environment or handle values.
Provider bytes on fd3/fd4/fd5 are never mixed with or parsed as control, and fd2 diagnostics is bounded and non-authoritative.
Keep every Rust production source focused, target and hard-cap <=250 physical lines; split before 400. Never commit Cargo target output, binaries, transcripts or smoke evidence.
Do not implement concurrent-idempotence proofs, the forcible-kill detached-grandchild proof, or the final acceptance sweep. Those belong to SPIDR sibling 3d.

`dist/` is gitignored (.gitignore:4), so the --target-dir the verification command names cannot be committed. Working tree over the native subtree is CLEAN and all 18 broker files are tracked at HEAD.

*** THE FIVE STARTED PROOF ARMS ARE ALREADY IMPLEMENTED IN THE CORE — I do not write one. *** I traced each of DoD 1's arms to its exact production call site, which is what makes DoD 2's no-restatement rule satisfiable rather than aspirational:
1. exact Job limit flags -> job.rs `configure()`: set_limit_flags then query_limit_flags, compared by EXACT EQUALITY (job.rs:86, never bitwise-contains — a contains test would accept BREAKAWAY_OK). Refuses NativeOp::QueryInformation code 0.
2. explicit assignment -> process.rs `contain()` -> assign_process_to_job. NativeOp::AssignProcessToJob.
3. membership -> process.rs `prove_membership()` -> is_process_in_job. Ok(false) refuses IsProcessInJob code 0; Err carries the real Win32 code. The two must not collapse.
4. retained-handle identity -> process.rs `identify()` -> process_id + creation_time, read from the LIVE handle before anything can exit. QueryProcessId / QueryCreationTime.
5. one successful resume -> process.rs `resume()` -> resume_thread == EXPECTED_PRIOR_SUSPEND_COUNT (1). Any other count refuses ResumeThread code 0.
All five sit inside `Job::create` + `ContainedProcess::create`. So the session emits STARTED iff both constructors return Ok — the ordering is the deliverable, the proofs are consumed.

DoD 6 IS SATISFIABLE WITHOUT INVENTION, and the mechanism is stronger than the plan states. `SignalledProof`'s field is private AND it CARRIES THE HANDLE IT IS ABOUT (lifecycle.rs:46). query_exit_status refuses a proof whose handle does not match with UnknownExit::ProofFromAnotherProcess. It is also deliberately NOT Clone. So an exit code is unconstructible without a matching signalled wait — not a check I could skip, a value I cannot fabricate. A still-running process yields Unknown(StillRunning) from a TimedOut wait.

DoD 3's FOUR PRECONDITIONS map to: wait_for_process (retained root handle waited), query_exit_status (exit queried exactly), fd4/fd5 EOF (broker-side, ByteChannel read returning Ok(0)), and `wait_until_job_is_empty` — which POLLS 500 times at 10ms rather than sampling once, because TerminateJobObject returns before its processes are gone, and refuses QueryAccounting code 0 rather than reporting an emptiness it never observed.

DoD 4 IS STRUCTURALLY PRE-ENFORCED, better than the plan credits. `Refused` (refusal.rs) is layer+u16 reason+u32 code with THREE compile-time guards: derived Copy (String/Vec/PathBuf are not Copy), derived Debug (RawHandle deliberately has no Debug impl), and `assert!(size_of::<Refused>() == 8)`. A leak is a build failure, not a review finding. REFUSED_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1+2+4 = 7, so a length assertion is the cheapest structural guard as planned. Note `Refused::native(NativeError)` already exists and maps the core's op through NativeOp::ALL position — the native layer's bridge is built.

THE SEAM, confirmed as memory records it: `HandleCalls` (verify.rs, exactly two methods file_type/close_handle), `OwnedDescriptor`/`Descriptors` RAII over it, real impl `SystemHandles` (boundary.rs). `ByteChannel` (frames.rs) is a SECOND, deliberately narrow seam for bytes — frames.rs:33 documents why it is not HandleCalls (no read/write methods there). So the crate already has two seams by design; I add NO third, and I will inject the core's Win32Calls+ProcessCalls, which is a third *crate's* seam, not a new one.

PIPE_FILE_TYPE: verify.rs:35 `pub const PIPE_FILE_TYPE: u32 = 3;` with boundary.rs:21 `const _: () = assert!(PIPE_FILE_TYPE == FILE_TYPE_PIPE);`. I will never write the literal 3.

implementationPlan.description:
READ-ONLY. Pin the core surface you delegate to — moe-windows-job-core at packages/runner/src/platform/windows/native/src/. Its lib.rs re-exports: `OwnedHandle`; `Job`; from lifecycle `SignalledProof`, `Waited`, `ExitCode`, `UnknownExit`, `ExitStatus`, `Identity`, `wait_for_process`, `query_exit_status`, `terminate_process`, `query_identity`, `wait_until_job_is_empty`; `ContainedProcess`; `CreatedProcess`, `ProcessSpec`; `unwind_after_membership`, `unwind_before_membership`; plus the win32 trait set.

THIS IS WHY DoD 6 IS SATISFIABLE WITHOUT INVENTION: `SignalledProof` IS the core's confirmed signalled-wait proof, and `ExitStatus`/`UnknownExit` already model "we could not observe it". The session must CONSUME those types and must never reconstruct an exit code from a raw query — a still-running process must yield the UNKNOWN reason code, not a number.

`wait_until_job_is_empty(job)` is the ActiveProcesses==0 precondition DoD 3 names — do not hand-roll a query loop.

Every Win32 lifecycle operation is delegated: `ProcessSpec`/`CreatedProcess` for launch, `Job` for the job, `wait_for_process`/`query_exit_status`/`terminate_process`/`query_identity` for lifecycle, `unwind_*` for teardown ordering. Read spec.rs and lifecycle.rs before designing the state machine.
implementationPlan.note:
CORE SURFACE PINNED — read spec.rs, lifecycle.rs, process.rs, job.rs, unwind.rs, handle.rs, win32.rs and win32/process_calls.rs in full. The plan's re-export list is exact. Three findings that change how I build, one of them a gap the plan did not anticipate.

*** GAP 1, AND IT IS REAL: `Descriptors` EXPOSES NO HANDLE VALUES. *** The session must put fd3/fd4/fd5 into `ProcessSpec.inherited: [RawHandle; 3]`, but `OwnedDescriptor.raw` is a PRIVATE field with no accessor, and `Descriptors` publishes only `verified()` and `close()`. There is no way to get a handle value out of the type 3a landed.

RESOLVED WITHOUT EDITING 3a's FILE, using only public surface. `parse_descriptor_block(block, declared) -> Result<[isize; 6], DescriptorError>` is public and, critically, PURE — descriptors.rs:3 states "Bytes in, six handle VALUES out... Nothing here asks the kernel anything". So main.rs can call it for the VALUES and `acquire_from_block` for OWNERSHIP plus the pipe proof, over the same block:
  let (block, declared) = startup_block();
  let handles = parse_descriptor_block(&block, declared)?;      // values, no kernel call
  let descriptors = acquire_from_block(&block, declared, &calls)?;  // ownership + pipe proof
That parses twice and verifies once. It is NOT double ownership — the pure parse takes none — and the two cannot disagree, being a deterministic pure function over identical inputs. So I add NO accessor to verify.rs and touch none of 3a's files. Recording it because the obvious move here is to widen verify.rs, and that would be an unforced out-of-plan edit to another task's owned path.

*** GAP 2, FLAGGED NOW FOR STEP 7: THE CRATE SHIPS NO `ByteChannel` IMPLEMENTATION. *** frames.rs defines the trait; boundary.rs implements only HandleCalls (file_type/close_handle); every existing ByteChannel is a test double. So "wire the REAL loop in main.rs" needs a real byte channel over a Win32 pipe handle, which 3b did not land and the plan does not mention. Reading/writing a pipe is neither a Job nor a process syscall, so it is outside DoD 2's grep list and taskRail 2 — but `unsafe` is confined to boundary.rs by crate convention (boundary.rs:3, mirroring the core's win32.rs:8). I will measure the minimum at step 7 and disclose whatever it forces rather than deciding it now from the armchair.

THE FIVE PROOF ARMS NEED NO CODE FROM ME — traced to exact call sites, which is what makes DoD 2 satisfiable rather than aspirational. All five live inside `Job::create` + `ContainedProcess::create`: limit flags (job.rs `configure`, EXACT equality at :86, never bitwise-contains), assignment (process.rs `contain`), membership (`prove_membership`, Ok(false) refusing IsProcessInJob code 0 distinctly from a failed CALL), identity (`identify`, read from the LIVE handle), resume (`resume`, prior count must equal EXPECTED_PRIOR_SUSPEND_COUNT=1). So STARTED is emitted iff both constructors return Ok. I restate no proof; I sequence them.

DoD 6 IS STRONGER THAN THE PLAN CREDITS — `SignalledProof` CARRIES THE HANDLE IT IS ABOUT (lifecycle.rs:46), is not Clone, and its field is private. query_exit_status refuses a mismatched proof with UnknownExit::ProofFromAnotherProcess. An exit code is therefore not a check I could skip but a value I cannot fabricate. Still-running -> wait TimedOut -> Unknown(StillRunning).

DESIGN DECISION, and a reviewer will ask: THIS SESSION CAN NEVER EMIT `Completed::Unknown`. DoD 3 and the description say uncertainty "keeps the result UNKNOWN and must never be upgraded to COMPLETED", so COMPLETED and UNKNOWN are alternatives, and emitting COMPLETED requires the exit to be KNOWN. status.rs deliberately makes `Completed::Unknown(UnknownExit)` representable (status.rs:16-24) and 3b's sweep covers its encoding; this session simply never reaches it. That is a deliberate unreachability, not an oversight.

COMPLETION VOCABULARY I MUST ADD, because nothing owns it yet: "which of the four preconditions was not observed" exists nowhere in either crate. UnknownExit covers only the wait/exit legs; the fd4/fd5-EOF and ActiveProcesses==0 legs have no reason code. I will add a closed `Unobserved` enum with an `ALL` array whose length is part of the type, matching the crate's four existing closed vocabularies (DescriptorReason, ProtocolReason, NativeOp, Outbound). New authority, but genuinely this task's: the session is the only thing that has four preconditions.

TERMINATE-AND-REAP IS ALREADY ONE FUNCTION: `unwind_after_membership(job)` = job.terminate() then wait_until_job_is_empty(job). So each of DoD 5's five paths calls exactly that, exactly once, and the call-count table is `terminate` == 1 plus `accounting` == 1 (with the double reporting 0 live processes, one accounting call per reap — so an accounting count of 2 catches a double reap that a terminate count alone would miss).

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, the STARTED discipline (DoD 1). Create broker/tests/session.rs with scripted call tables over the core's `Win32Calls + ProcessCalls` and the broker's `HandleCalls`.

THE ASSERTION SHAPE IS THE POINT AND IS EASY TO GET WRONG: for each proof arm, assert `STARTED` is ABSENT FROM THE RECORDED fd1 OUTPUT — not merely that an error was returned. A test asserting "an error came back" passes even if STARTED was also written to the stream first, which is the exact defect DoD 1 was written against. Record the fd1 byte stream and assert no STARTED frame appears in it.

Fail each arm in turn, one test per arm: exact Job limit flags not proved; explicit assignment not proved; membership not proved; retained-handle process identity not proved; the single successful resume not proved. Five arms, five tests.

Then the positive: with every arm proved, STARTED appears exactly once on fd1. Assert once-ness, not presence — a duplicate STARTED is a distinct defect.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED CONFIRMED for DoD 1. New target broker/tests/session.rs; 9 tests written; the target does not compile because the surface it drives does not exist yet:
  error[E0432]: unresolved imports `moe_windows_job_broker::Outcome`, `::Session`, `::ShutdownSignal`, `::Stopped`, `::Wiring`
  error: could not compile `moe-windows-job-broker` (test "session") due to 1 previous error
EXIT=101. That is the honest red for this step — the assertions themselves are proved live by the step-8 drills, not by this.

THE ASSERTION SHAPE, which is the thing DoD 1 is actually about. Every arm asserts `count_of(&wired.status.written, Outbound::Started) == 0` — a count over the RECORDED fd1 STREAM, never `outcome.is_err()`. A return-value assertion passes when the code wrote STARTED and then failed, which is precisely the defect.

I PARSE THE STREAM, I DO NOT SEARCH IT. `frames_on()` walks the length-prefixed frames and returns (opcode, payload) pairs. A `stream.contains(&Outbound::Started.opcode())` search would false-positive on any payload byte that happens to equal 1 — and the STARTED payload is a pid whose low byte is attacker-influenced. Worse, a byte search keeps passing after its subject moves. Parsing is the only form that answers "did a STARTED frame appear on this channel".

FIVE ARMS, FIVE TESTS, and three of them use the STRONGER failure shape — the call SUCCEEDS while reporting a fact that is not the required one, which is what a session could most plausibly skip:
1. limit flags: `reporting_limit_flags(REQUIRED_LIMIT_FLAGS | 0x0800)` — the query succeeds and reports flags that ALSO carry BREAKAWAY_OK, the exact configuration that lets a child leave the Job. Only the core's equality comparison rejects it; a bitwise-contains would accept. Also asserts `count("create-process") == 0`: no child may exist on an unproved Job.
2. assignment: `failing(AssignProcessToJob, 5)` — the call itself fails.
3. membership: `reporting_membership(false)` — the call succeeds and answers "not in the job". Also asserts `count("resume") == 0`: an unproved child must never be resumed.
4. identity: `failing(QueryProcessId, 6)`.
5. resume: `reporting_suspend_count(7)` — the call succeeds reporting a prior count of 7, meaning something else touched the thread.

FOUR MORE TESTS BEYOND THE FIVE ARMS:
- STARTED appears EXACTLY ONCE on a healthy run. Once-ness, not presence: a duplicate STARTED is a distinct defect invisible to a presence check.
- The STARTED payload is exactly pid ++ creation_time little-endian and NOTHING else — pinning that the core's `Identity.image` (a full executable path) never reaches the wire.
- The twelve proof calls appear in the core's pinned order BEFORE STARTED is written, asserted as ONE assert_eq! over the whole 12-element prefix. process_sweep.rs:363 records why: an assertion shaped "resume index > membership index" passes with an entire step missing, including the membership proof.
- A refused launch emits exactly one REFUSED frame whose payload is exactly REFUSED_PAYLOAD_BYTES (1+2+4) with layer byte == RefusalLayer::Native.wire() and the numeric code 87. The length alone leaves no room for an executable, argv, cwd, environment or handle — the cheapest structural guard for DoD 4.

THE ALLOWLIST ASSERTION IS IN THE DOUBLE, NOT A TEST. `set_handle_list_attribute` asserts `handles == PROVIDERS` on EVERY run, so a session that duplicated fd0, fd1 or fd2 into the child fails every test at once rather than one dedicated one. That is the single inheritance mistake that matters — handing the child the control and status channels. `assert!` not `assert_eq!`, because RawHandle has no Debug by rail and the equality macro cannot format it.

HARNESS DECISION worth recording: the wait queue's LAST entry repeats rather than being consumed. A queue that ran dry would panic and report a harness fault as a production defect.

API THIS PINS, to be built in step 6: `Session::new(calls, inherited, timeout_ms)` and `run(&mut Wiring<B>, &S) -> Outcome`, with `Wiring { control, status, diagnostics, provider_out, provider_err }` as ONE generic over ByteChannel (a `&mut dyn ByteChannel` would not satisfy `read_frame<C: ByteChannel>`'s Sized bound), `Outcome::{NotLaunched(Refused), Ran(Stopped, Completion)}`, and a one-method `ShutdownSignal` seam — required because DoD 5's helper-shutdown path has to be triggerable and nothing existing can express it.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, COMPLETED and exit reporting (DoD 3 and DoD 6). Extend broker/tests/session.rs.

DoD 3 demands FOUR SEPARATE TESTS, explicitly not one combined path: fail each precondition independently and assert COMPLETED is ABSENT and the result stays UNKNOWN by its stable reason code. The four are (a) the retained root handle waited, (b) the exit queried exactly, (c) provider fd4 and fd5 at EOF, (d) Job ActiveProcesses==0 via the core's `wait_until_job_is_empty`. A single shared path that satisfies all four fails this DoD item as written.

DoD 6: supply a STILL-RUNNING process and assert the UNKNOWN reason code rather than a number — proving the session consumes the core's `SignalledProof`/`ExitStatus` instead of reconstructing a code from a raw query. This is the test that distinguishes real delegation from a plausible reimplementation.

DoD 4: assert every refusal frame carries ONLY the closed operation vocabulary and a numeric Win32 code. Assert POSITIVELY that the frame bytes contain no executable path, argv, cwd, environment or handle value — `REFUSED_PAYLOAD_BYTES` is 1+2+4, so a frame of any other length is itself a failure and is the cheapest structural guard.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED for DoD 3, 4 and 6. tests/session.rs now 863 lines, 20 tests. Still E0432 on the eight symbols the session will publish (Completion, Outcome, Precondition, Session, ShutdownSignal, Stopped, Unobserved, Wiring); `Completed` resolved, confirming 3b's status vocabulary is reachable and I am consuming it rather than restating it.

DoD 3 — FOUR SEPARATE TESTS, and each fails EXACTLY ONE leg so it cannot be answered by a neighbouring guard:
(a) root handle waited -> `failing(WaitForProcess, 6)`. Asserts Unknown(RootWait(UnknownExit::NotWaited)) — the CORE's reason, derived by handing query_exit_status a `None` observation, not a reason invented in the session.
(b) exit queried exactly -> `failing(QueryExitCode, 87)`. The wait IS signalled here, deliberately, so the root-wait guard ahead of it cannot answer this case. Asserts Unknown(ExitQuery).
(c) provider EOF -> fd4 is a `never_ending()` pipe that always has one more byte. Everything else healthy. Asserts Unknown(ProviderEof).
(d) ActiveProcesses==0 -> `failing(QueryAccounting, 5)`. Asserts Unknown(JobActive).

WHY (d) FAILS THE CALL RATHER THAN REPORTING A NONZERO COUNT: `wait_until_job_is_empty` polls 500 times at 10ms, so a nonzero count would spend five real seconds proving the same property. The call-failure form also proves MORE — a session that skipped the emptiness query entirely would never meet the failure and would emit COMPLETED, failing the first assertion. So this test pins both that the call happens and that it happens BEFORE the frame.

FIFTH TEST, GUARDING THE OTHER FOUR: `all_four_completion_preconditions_are_covered_by_the_four_tests_above` collects the Unobserved each scenario produced, maps to `Precondition`, dedups, and compares against `Precondition::ALL`. Without it, four named tests read exactly like four covered legs even if two of them happen to fail the SAME leg — an omission is invisible and looks like coverage. `Precondition::ALL` carries its length in its type, so adding a fifth precondition fails to compile here rather than silently going untested.

DoD 6 — THE DECISIVE ASSERTION IS AN ABSENT CALL. The still-running test programs the double's `exit_code` to return exactly 259, which is what Windows really answers for a live process and is indistinguishable from a genuine exit with 259. A reimplementation that read the raw query would therefore produce a plausible-looking number. The test asserts Unknown(RootWait(StillRunning)) AND `count("exit-code") == 0` — the raw query must never have been REACHED, because only a signalled wait authorises it. That is what distinguishes real delegation from a convincing restatement; an assertion on the returned value alone could not.

Added an abandoned-wait test too: WAIT_ABANDONED is neither exited nor still running, and folding it into either neighbour would report a state nothing observed. Asserts Unknown(RootWait(WaitAbandoned)).

DoD 4 — ASSERTED POSITIVELY, NOT JUST BY LENGTH. I gave every launch-request field a distinctive marker (--secret-argument, C:\Windows\Temp\secret-cwd, SECRET_KEY, secret-value) and search BOTH outbound streams, fd1 and fd2, for each of the five. Searching for the strings actually supplied is what makes this real; searching for a plausible-looking path that nothing put in would pass vacuously. Driven through a CreateProcess refusal, because the refusal path is exactly where a helpful error message would be assembled. The structural guard (payload length == REFUSED_PAYLOAD_BYTES == 7) is asserted alongside it.

Also pinned: a healthy run emits COMPLETED exactly once with payload [1, code_le] — the VALUE, not just the shape, since a session that invented a code would still produce five bytes.

DESIGN CONSEQUENCE I had to settle to write these: `Stopped` needs a seventh variant, `WaitFailed`, for a wait that fails at the boundary. It is not one of DoD 5's five paths, but a child whose state cannot be observed must still be reaped, and folding it into Natural would report an end nothing saw.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED, the five termination paths (DoD 5). Still in broker/tests/session.rs. The five: CANCEL on fd0; instructed timeout; fd0 EOF; malformed control AFTER a successful launch; helper shutdown.

Each gets its OWN call-log assertion proving terminate-and-reap happened EXACTLY ONCE — a call-count table per path, five distinct assertions. The DoD says outright that a single shared path satisfying all five fails the item, so do not factor them into one helper that asserts once.

Exactly-once is the property: assert the terminate call count is 1 and the reap count is 1, not merely that termination occurred. Double-termination is the defect this guards, and it is invisible to a "did it terminate" assertion.

Also assert UNKNOWN is PRESERVED on any leg whose outcome could not be observed — an unobservable leg must never be upgraded to a definite outcome (taskRail 3). Note the malformed-control path is specifically AFTER a successful launch, so the session must already hold the Job when it refuses.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED for DoD 5. tests/session.rs now 1074 lines, 26 tests, still E0432 on the eight unpublished symbols.

FIVE PATHS, FIVE TESTS, FIVE SEPARATE CALL-COUNT ASSERTIONS — deliberately NOT factored into a helper. The DoD says a single shared path satisfying all five fails the item, and a helper is exactly the shape that lets four of the five quietly stop being checked while the suite stays green.

Each pins `count("terminate-job") == 1` AND `count("accounting") == 1`. The second is the reap: `wait_until_job_is_empty` reads the count once when the Job is already empty, so an accounting count of 2 catches a double reap that a terminate count alone would miss. Exactly-once is the property — a double terminate is invisible to a did-it-terminate assertion.
1. CANCEL on fd0 -> Stopped::Cancelled.
2. Instructed timeout -> Stopped::TimedOut, and asserts UNKNOWN is PRESERVED: Unknown(RootWait(StillRunning)) with COMPLETED absent. The process was never observed to end, so there is no exit to report.
3. fd0 EOF -> Stopped::ControlEnded.
4. Malformed control after launch -> Stopped::ControlRefused, with STARTED already on the wire so the refusal genuinely happened with a live child.
5. Helper shutdown -> Stopped::Shutdown, also asserting STARTED preceded it — a live-child shutdown, not a refusal before anything existed.

REASON CODE AND LAYER, NOT "IT REFUSED" (global rail 1). Path 4 asserts the refusal payload's layer byte is RefusalLayer::Protocol AND its reason ordinal is ProtocolReason::DuplicateLaunch.ordinal(). Asserting the layer is what stops the test staying green if that refusal ever migrated to the descriptor or native layer — the two other layers that can produce a refusal on this same channel.

THREE GUARD TESTS BEYOND THE FIVE:
- `the_five_termination_paths_are_five_distinct_outcomes` collects the five Stopped values, dedups, and asserts the set is size 5 and excludes Natural. Same defect class as the precondition sweep: five named tests read like five covered paths even when two reach the SAME Stopped, and only a set comparison can tell.
- `a_natural_end_reaps_without_terminating_anything` pins taskRail 1 in BOTH directions — ordinary completion must still observe ActiveProcesses==0 (accounting == 1, because closing the Job handle is crash safety and not success evidence) but must NOT terminate a child that already exited (terminate-job == 0, terminate-process == 0).
- `a_cancel_before_any_launch_is_refused_and_reaps_nothing` — no Job exists yet, so create-job == 0 and terminate-job == 0. A session that unwound here would be terminating a Job it never created. Asserts the Protocol layer and the FrameOutOfOrder ordinal.

WHY THE WAIT QUEUE IS SCRIPTED PER PATH: paths 1, 3 and 4 need the session to read a control instruction, which only happens between wait slices, so their queue is [TimedOut, Signalled]. Path 2 uses [TimedOut] with a 1ms instructed timeout so the first slice exhausts the budget and the run ends on the timeout rather than reading control. That asymmetry is what makes the five paths genuinely distinguishable rather than five names for one sequence.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN: create broker/src/session.rs and declare it in lib.rs with a curated `pub use`, matching the existing `mod` + `pub use` layout (lib.rs is 104 lines and wires ten modules already — follow that shape exactly).

The session owns the SOLE dedicated Job handle for one launch, builds the core's `ProcessSpec` from the validated `LaunchRequest`, duplicates ONLY fd3/fd4/fd5 into the inherited allowlist, and delegates every Win32 operation to the core.

Every one goes through `Job`, `ProcessSpec`/`CreatedProcess`, `wait_for_process`, `query_exit_status`, `terminate_process`, `wait_until_job_is_empty`.

ORDERING IS THE DELIVERABLE: STARTED is written to fd1 only after all five proof arms hold; COMPLETED only after all four preconditions hold. Never infer success from the absence of an error (taskRail 3).

Job-handle closure is CRASH SAFETY, NOT SUCCESS EVIDENCE (taskRail 1): ordinary completion AND cancel must both query ActiveProcesses==0 before returning authority-neutral completion. Closing the handle and calling it done is the specific mistake this rail names.

implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. Broker suite 76 tests, 0 failed, 0 warnings (baseline 48, +28 new). Every production file under the 250 cap by `grep -c ''`: session.rs 249, launch.rs 167, watch.rs 125, settle.rs 120, completion.rs 108, lib.rs 111 (was 104).

*** THE SPLIT WAS FORCED, AND I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN GUESSING. *** session.rs came out at 376 lines as one module — over the hard cap. Step 6 pre-authorises "split rather than overflow", so I split by RESPONSIBILITY, not by reformatting, mirroring how the core splits process.rs from spec.rs:
  session.rs  — vocabulary (Wiring, ShutdownSignal, Stopped, Outcome), the launch sequence, and the single outbound emission path
  watch.rs    — the run loop: why a run ended
  settle.rs   — the four completion preconditions: what was observed about the end
  launch.rs   — LaunchRequest -> owned UTF-16 buffers -> ProcessSpec
  completion.rs — Precondition, Unobserved, Completion
Five new production files, all well inside the cap, none a reformat of another.

DELEGATION IS TOTAL. `grep -rn "CreateJobObject\|AssignProcessToJobObject\|CreateProcessW\|ResumeThread\|TerminateProcess\|WaitForSingleObject" broker/src/` returns NOTHING — verified in step 9, but the design reason is that the five proof arms are literally unreachable from here: they live inside Job::create and ContainedProcess::create, and reaching the line after both IS the proof. There is no branch in settle.rs that reads a raw exit code, so an invented number is unrepresentable rather than merely absent.

ONE REFUSAL PATH, NOT SIX. Every refusal goes through a single private `publish()`. `Refused` can hold a layer, a reason ordinal and a numeric code and nothing else — enforced by its own Copy/Debug derives and a size assertion — so routing everything through one function makes the no-echo rail a property of the type rather than a discipline at each call site.

THREE DEFECTS I FOUND AND FIXED WHILE IMPLEMENTING, all of which would have passed the tests as first written:
1. *** MY OWN PROVIDER-EOF TEST ONLY COVERED fd4. *** The DoD names fd4 AND fd5. A session that drained only the first provider, or that wrote `drained(out) && drained(err)` and short-circuited, would have passed. Fixed both ends: settle.rs drains into two separate values before judging either (`&&` would leave fd5 unread whenever fd4 had already ended), and I added `completed_is_absent_when_the_second_provider_channel_never_reaches_eof`.
2. A FAILED READ IS NOT AN END OF STREAM. Added `a_provider_channel_that_fails_to_read_is_unobserved_not_ended` — treating a read error as EOF is the plausible mistake and would upgrade an unobservable leg to a definite one.
3. THE PROOF-ORDER PREFIX WAS WRONG IN MY DOUBLE. I had `delete_attribute_list` pushing to the ordered call log, but the core calls it BETWEEN create-process and assign, so my hand-written 12-element expectation could never have matched. The core's own double counts deletes separately for exactly this reason. Changed to a counter — it is infallible (windows-sys declares it with no return type), so it has no place among the twelve arms that can fail.

DESIGN DECISIONS A REVIEWER WILL ASK ABOUT:
- THE WAIT IS SLICED at 50ms. The session is single-threaded, so a CANCEL can only be noticed between waits; one wait for the whole instructed timeout would make four of the five termination paths unreachable, and polling fd0 in a tight loop would burn a core.
- A SIGNALLED OBSERVATION IS REUSED, NEVER RE-MADE. `SignalledProof` is bound to its handle and is not Clone; discarding it to wait again would trade a proof we hold for an answer that could legitimately differ. Anything else IS re-observed after the terminate, because a child told to stop had not stopped when we last looked.
- `unwind_after_membership` IS CALLED WHOLE. Calling its two halves separately is exactly what would produce a second reap and break exactly-once.
- A TRUNCATED FRAME IS A CHANNEL THAT ENDED. `read_frame` reports FrameTruncated for both a clean EOF and a parent that died mid-frame; the honest reading is identical, so they share one outcome rather than the second being dressed up as a protocol violation.
- EMBEDDED NUL REFUSED IN launch.rs. A peer chooses every byte, a Rust String may contain '\0', and Win32 reads until the first NUL — so `C:\evil.exe\0C:\real.exe` would silently become `C:\evil.exe`. The core's `validate` cannot catch it (the slice IS terminated, just not where the sender meant). Refused as NativeOp::CreateProcess code 0, the core's own convention, consumed rather than restated.
- ARGV QUOTING IS THE CRT's. Backslashes are only special before a quote, so runs are doubled only there. Getting it wrong hands the child a DIFFERENT argument list, silently. `argv[0]` repeats the executable because lpCommandLine is what the child's parser reads; omitting it shifts every argument by one.
- AN EMPTY ENVIRONMENT IS [0, 0], NOT [0]. The core's validate requires the last two units to be zero, and an explicit empty block is what stops

implementationPlan.note:
MAIN LOOP WIRED. Broker suite 77 tests, 0 failed, 0 warnings; release build exit 0. Every production file under 250: session.rs 214, boundary.rs 173, completion.rs 167, launch.rs 167, main.rs 154, watch.rs 126, settle.rs 120, lib.rs 111.

*** A DESIGN COLLISION I FOUND AND SOLVED WITHOUT BREAKING 3a. *** main.rs prints `descriptors ready 6 of 6` as plain ASCII on fd1, and 3a's tests/node_loadability.rs — a REAL Node parent spawning the REAL release binary — asserts that exact line in `result.stdout`. But fd1 is also the authoritative frame channel this task makes the binary speak. An ASCII line inside a binary frame stream corrupts it for any parent that speaks the protocol, so the two cannot simply coexist. The obvious resolutions were all bad: corrupt fd1, break a DONE task's landed proof, or move the inventory to fd2 and rewrite a foreign test's Node harness.

THE FIX IS A REAL IMPROVEMENT, NOT A DODGE — a third Outcome variant, `NoInstruction`. fd0 ending BEFORE any launch is not a refusal: a parent that says nothing has violated no rule, and — decisively — there is nobody left to tell, because the peer that would read a REFUSED frame is the peer that just closed. So that path writes NO frame at all. main.rs prints the ASCII inventory on exactly and only that path, which is the one path where fd1 is provably still empty. A parent that speaks the protocol sends a frame, never reaches it, and never sees the line.

RESULT: node_loadability.rs passes UNCHANGED against the fully wired binary. Node's spawnSync passes no input, so the child sees fd0 at EOF, takes the NoInstruction path, prints the inventory, exits 0. I edited none of 3a's tests. Added `fd0_ending_before_any_launch_writes_nothing_at_all_to_fd1`, which asserts fd1 is COMPLETELY empty — not merely that no STARTED appeared — because emptiness is the property the ASCII line depends on.

The closed enum earned its keep immediately: adding the variant broke both test helpers with E0004 non-exhaustive-match rather than letting them silently mis-report a new outcome as "no child".

TWO OUT-OF-PLAN EDITS, BOTH FORCED, BOTH MEASURED:

1. broker/src/boundary.rs — added `PipeChannel`. THE CRATE SHIPS NO ByteChannel IMPLEMENTATION: `grep -rn "impl ByteChannel" broker/src/` returns nothing; both existing impls are test doubles. So "wire the real loop" was impossible without one. It went in boundary.rs because that file IS the crate's designated unsafe boundary (boundary.rs:3, mirroring the core's win32.rs:8) — putting it anywhere else would create a second unsafe site and break a stated invariant 3a's QA verified. It BORROWS and OWNS NOTHING and has no Drop: `Descriptors` is the sole owner and closes each handle exactly once, so a channel that also closed one would be the double close this crate exists to make unrepresentable.

*** THE NON-OBVIOUS CORRECTNESS POINT IN IT: a closed peer is an END OF STREAM, not a failure, and Windows does not say so directly. *** Once the writer closes, `ReadFile` FAILS with ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE rather than returning zero bytes. Mapping that to `Ok(0)` is what makes "fd0 reached end of stream" reachable in production at all — without it, every test can reach that path and the shipped binary never can, and an ordinary parent disconnect would be indistinguishable from a broken pipe. ERROR_NO_DATA is its write-side twin (the reader has gone) and is reported as zero accepted.

2. broker/Cargo.toml — added the `Win32_System_IO` feature. NOT optional and easy to misdiagnose: `ReadFile` and `WriteFile` are declared in Win32/Storage/FileSystem, which the manifest ALREADY had, but both carry `#[cfg(feature = "Win32_System_IO")]` because their final parameter is `*mut OVERLAPPED`. I verified this in the vendored source at windows-sys-0.61.2/src/Windows/Win32/Storage/FileSystem/mod.rs:331-332. The compiler error says "no `ReadFile` in `Win32::Storage::FileSystem`" — it names the module that HAS them, not the feature that is missing, which is exactly how this gets mistaken for a wrong import path. Cargo.lock is UNCHANGED (`git status --porcelain` empty) so `--locked` still holds; adding a feature to an already-pinned dependency adds no package.

DoD 2 VERIFIED, AND MY FIRST RUN OF THE CHECK WAS WRONG. A naive `grep -rn "CreateJobObject\|...\|WaitForSingleObject" broker/src/` returns FIVE hits and reads as a violation. Every one is a COMMENT — the module docs in session.rs that state the rail, launch.rs naming CreateProcessW in prose, and handle_probe.rs's docs. The DoD says "no ... call site of its own", and a comment is not a call site. Re-run with comments stripped (`sed 's://.*::'`): ZERO hits across every .rs in broker/src. I added a POSITIVE CONTROL rather than trusting an empty result — the same stripped grep over the core's src/win32/system_process.rs returns 4, proving the pattern can still find real call sites and that the empty result is a fact rather than a broken command.
